newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville offers 300 MW firm peak power for Mon.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville offers 300 MW firm peak power for Mon.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) offered 300 megawatts (MW) of firm, peak electricity for delivery Monday at $31.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), the federal agency said Wednesday.
Peak power in the Northwest for Monday was being offered at $32.00, while peak power at the California Oregon Border (COB) was being offered at $32.75, BPA said.
Light-load power for Monday was being offered at $22.25 and at $23.00 for the Northwest and COB, with a 300 MW limit, the agency said.
For Sunday, BPA was offering peak power, with a 500 MW limit, at $29.50 and at $30.00 in the Northwest and $30.75 at COB.
For light load hours on Sunday, BPA was offering up to 300 MW at $21.25 and at $22.00 in the Northwest and COB, the agency said.
BPA had said Tuesday that for Friday and Saturday it was offering up to 300 MW of peak load power at $31.50 per MWh.
